explain.3: Make the shared chat: an empty list. Every message will be added to the end of it.
explain.4: A list of who the LLM wrote for. Each LLM write adds a name, so len(calls) counts the writes.
explain.6: Define post: it adds one message to the chat. Nothing runs yet; it runs each time a message is posted.
explain.7: Make the message, a dictionary with who wrote it and what it says, and add it to the end of the chat.
explain.8: Show the message on screen, like a line in a group chat.
explain.10: The team: three bot names, in a list.
explain.11: Each bot's own instructions, in a dictionary: name → instructions.
explain.17: Define text_for: the text one bot reads, found by the bot's name.
explain.18: Start with this bot's own instructions, an empty line, and a heading for the chat.
explain.19: Go through every message in the chat, in order.
explain.20: Add the message as one line: who, a colon, then what they said.
explain.21: End with this bot's name and a colon, so the LLM writes as this bot.
explain.22: Glue all the lines together into one text, one per line, and hand it back.
explain.25: Define fresh_replies: it hands back a new dictionary of fake replies, so every run starts full.
explain.26: Hand back the fake replies: bot name → its replies, in order.
explain.33: Define the fake LLM. It takes the bot's name and the text it reads.
explain.34: Count this write: add the bot's name to calls.
explain.35: Take this bot's next reply off its list and hand it back.
explain.38: Define way 1: find who is @mentioned in a message.
explain.39: Start an empty list of names.
explain.40: Go through every bot name, in the team's order.
explain.41: Is @ followed by this name (like @Production) inside the message?
explain.42: Yes: add this bot to the ones who reply next.
explain.43: Hand back the names found. An empty list means no one was mentioned.
explain.45: Try it on one message: only Production is mentioned.
explain.49: Define way 2: a coordinator decides who replies next.
explain.50: The coordinator is an LLM too: count its write.
explain.51: The fake coordinator's next answer: one name.
explain.52: Is the name one of the team's bots?
explain.53: Yes: that bot replies next. A list with one name.
explain.54: Not a bot's name (here, CEO): hand back an empty list, so the chat waits for the CEO.
explain.58: Define the chat loop. router is the way to pick who's next: by_mentions or by_coordinator.
explain.59: The CEO posts the task. It's the first message in the chat.
explain.60: One round each time, up to the round limit.
explain.61: Give the last message (chat[-1]) to the router. It hands back who replies next.
explain.63: Then stop and wait for the CEO. That's how the chat ends here.
